steps.summary: Router matched the question to `count_in_hazard` for 'drawn area'
steps.why: This step only extracts the tool call and its arguments from the model; no computation happens here.
Exposure vs risk is never guessed — the agent pauses and asks.

options.label: **Exposure** — which of your assets (roads, schools, hospitals, buildings) physically sit inside the flood zone, ranked from low to extreme severity. This is the simplest and fastest answer, and just shows the raw hazard footprint — no modelling of how vulnerable each place is.

**Risk, official precomputed** — the ready-made flood risk layer from the regional agency, which blends how severe it is with how vulnerable the people and buildings in each place are. Pick this when you want a fast, authoritative answer you can quote as-is.

**Risk, recomputed from layers** — the same kind of flood risk, but rebuilt here from the underlying data so you can adjust how much weight hazard versus each vulnerability factor carries. It takes a little longer to compute on the fly, and it has been checked to closely match the official layer — almost every place lands in the same severity class, and none differ by more than one.

steps.question_asked:
For **flood** in drawn area, how would you like me to answer?

**1)** **Exposure** — which of your assets (roads, schools, hospitals, buildings) physically sit inside the flood zone, ranked from low to extreme severity. This is the simplest and fastest answer, and just shows the raw hazard footprint — no modelling of how vulnerable each place is.

**2)** **Risk, official precomputed** — the ready-made flood risk layer from the regional agency, which blends how severe it is with how vulnerable the people and buildings in each place are. Pick this when you want a fast, authoritative answer you can quote as-is.

**3)** **Risk, recomputed from layers** — the same kind of flood risk, but rebuilt here from the underlying data so you can adjust how much weight hazard versus each vulnerability factor carries. It takes a little longer to compute on the fly, and it has been checked to closely match the official layer — almost every place lands in the same severity class, and none differ by more than one.

Reply with the number (1–3) — or tap an option below.
